name: Unslop
tagline: A Claude Code skill that finds and fixes the generic, AI-generated look in your interface, pass by pass.
sentence: Audits your AI-built interface for design slop - purple gradients, emoji labels, stock layouts - sets a direction, and fixes it screen by screen like a designer doing a review.

visual.alt: Before and after comparison of a dashboard interface. The left side shows a generic AI-generated design with purple gradients and glowing elements. The right side shows the same dashboard with clean typography, restrained colors, and professional spacing.
visual.caption: Before and after: the same dashboard, unslopped.

board.say: Your AI-built interface looks like every other AI-built interface - generic gradients, stock layouts, and copy that screams 'a machine made this.'
You type `/unslop this dashboard` in Claude Code (or `$unslop` in Codex).
Your project's interface code (React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind, plain HTML/CSS, or a live site URL).
The skill audits the screen, sets a design direction, and makes fixes in order.
steps: Audits the screen and lists each sign of 'slop' with its location
Sets a design direction - character, color moments, a signature detail - and shows it to you before changing anything
Makes passes in order: spacing, color, icons, copy, typography, layout, details, visuals, motion
Optionally generates a short video of the screen unslopping itself (needs Playwright and ffmpeg installed)

board.say: A designed interface instead of a generic one.

outputs.eg: Removes purple gradients, replaces emoji labels with proper icons, fixes uneven spacing
Before any edits, you see the proposed character, color palette, and signature detail - you can steer it

before: Every AI-built interface has the same purple gradient, centered hero, three-card layout, and emoji labels
You'd need to hire a designer or learn design yourself to fix the generic look
after: One command audits the slop, proposes a direction, and fixes it pass by pass
Works with your existing code - React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind, or plain HTML
uses_note: Unslop is 9 days old. No independent user reports have been published yet. Creator Damir Sokolovsky started the 'Unslopping series' on X.

coverage.title: Best Claude Code Skills for Vibe Coding

steps: Copy the skill to your Claude Code skills folder: `mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/`
In any project, type `/unslop this dashboard` and review the audit before it makes changes
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
Then: Clone the repo, copy the skill to `~/.claude/skills/unslop`, open a project with a UI, and type `/unslop this dashboard`. 10 minutes.

footprint.disk: The skill itself is just text files (a few KB). Optional: Playwright (a browser testing tool) and Chromium for snapshots and videos. ffmpeg (a video tool) for the story video.
footprint.memory: Runs inside Claude Code - no separate process.
footprint.runs_on: Anywhere Claude Code or Codex runs (macOS, Windows, Linux).

best_for: Anyone who builds interfaces with AI and wants them to look hand-designed
Non-designers who want a design review without hiring one
People who already use Claude Code and want a one-command design fix
skip_if: You already have a designer or a design system you follow
You don't use Claude Code or Codex - this skill only works inside those tools
You need full design control - Unslop applies its own design opinions

alternatives.line: 50 real design themes for building new pages from scratch, rather than fixing existing ones

watch: **10K stars on 12 commits.** Viral popularity on a very small codebase. The skill is just text files - there isn't much code to review.
**9 days old.** Real use beyond the creator's own examples has not been reported.
**Only works with Claude Code or Codex.** It's a skill (an instruction set), not a standalone tool.
**Generated visuals cost money.** If you ask it to generate scenes or objects (not just fix your code), it uses a paid service (fal, Replicate, or OpenAI) and asks before each generation.
**CC BY 4.0 license.** Requires attribution - not the MIT or Apache license most open-source tools use.
